tailMarker.note: Earliest tail-class species is PARFUM @7. The declared allergens (LINALOOL @17, LIMONENE @18, BENZYL SALICYLATE @20) and the preservatives (BENZOIC ACID @16, BENZYL ALCOHOL @19) all follow it, so the class order is consistent and this is not the 'Parfum at the end behind its allergens' convention. The base (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4, STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @5, GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6) outranks the marker. Coconut oil @10 and the guar polymer @12 sit in the tail as secondary species. CAPRYLYL GLYCOL @13 (a booster) sits above BENZOIC ACID @16, but both are below the marker, where order is arbitrary; that does not touch the marker species. tail_index-1 = GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6. (v0.6, E13) The establishing species for conditioning_level/weight_potential (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4, SAPDMA @5, GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6) all outrank the marker, so it is plausible; the tail oils and the guar polymer are below-marker extras and never flip it. The CAPRYLYL GLYCOL @13 / BENZOIC ACID @16 ordering lies wholly inside the tail and does not engage the booster limb (round-2 triage note).

conditioning_level.rationale: S2 fires (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2). S3 fires (ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4, R4a light, plus GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6, mid band; S3 counts all three lipid bands, E14). S1 fails, because STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE @5 is the only cationic surfactant above the tail. S2+S3 without S1 is moderate (R3). The boundary oil is not load-bearing for the value, which would still be moderate on S2 alone.
evidenceSignals: S3 ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4 + GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6
counterSignals: single cationic surfactant on the whole list
Macadamia @8, sunflower @9, coconut @10, coco-caprylate @11 are tail (no credit)

weight_potential.rationale: Re-derived under v0.6 (E14, 2026-10-06). GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6 is the only lipid above PARFUM @7 apart from the light ester ISOPROPYL MYRISTATE @4, and soy is a MID-band liquid plant triglyceride, not R4b. High is unavailable: the heavy-lipid core needs an R4b species above the marker and none is present (COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @10 is heavy but sits in the tail), so the dense base (CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, top three) has no core to complete. Low is unavailable too: above the marker the mid-band soy oil defeats leanness conjunct 1 (no R4b and no mid-band triglyceride above the marker), even though conjunct 2 (no silicone at all) and conjunct 3 (STEARAMIDOPROPYL DIMETHYLAMINE the only cationic on the full list) hold. A mid-band oil blocks low and never makes high, so the value is moderate. The soy oil sits at tail_index-1 and is load-bearing (without it all three leanness conjuncts hold and the value would be low), so confidence stays capped at moderate under E1; the counterfactual is now one step (moderate vs low), no longer extreme-to-extreme.
evidenceSignals: mid-band GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6 above the marker (boundary position): blocks low, cannot make high (E14)
no R4b heavy lipid above PARFUM @7 (no high core)
dense base CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2 present but has no R4b core to complete
counterSignals: the moderate call rests on one species at tail_index-1: without GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6 the formula would satisfy the low leanness test
COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @10 (heavy band) sits in the tail: no credit; would have completed a high core above the marker (candidate_below_tail, E13)

care_direction.rationale: No R5 protein, peptide or keratin species appears anywhere on the list. The care result comes from a coherent cetearyl/amidoamine/emollient base (IPM @4, soy oil @6), which is the moisture default. Reading (b) is impossible: there is no film or acid route above the tail and an R4 stack is present. The marker is plausible and there is no protein payload, no tail cluster and no competing leg.
evidenceSignals: emollient base IPM @4, GLYCINE SOJA OIL @6

repair_support_level.rationale: No R5 route and no named bond token appear anywhere, so only ordinary conditioning and lubrication remain. The INCI is verified and the marker plausible.

primary_focus.rationale: Repair, curl and colour have no route. Moisture fails criterion 1 (only GLYCERIN @3 is above the tail; CAPRYLYL GLYCOL @13 is a tail booster). Shine fails criterion 1: there is no above-tail silicone or polymer route (the guar polymer @12 is in the tail). The mid-band soy oil is not R4b (E14), so the low-lipid-load half of criterion 1 would hold, but the optical-route half does not. Smoothing would only reuse the rich R1+R4 base, which §6 rule 1 counts as one M1 observation, and detangling has no distinctive slip route. The verdict is nonspecific, which resolves to general. Claim role is not_applicable.
counterSignals: competing smoothing rejected: baseline M1 lipid/fatty base only

secondary_focus.rationale: No route clears its own threshold. The single-glycerin humectant leg is not a cluster, so the E10 moisture secondary is unavailable.
